title: Man. Post. Cap. VI: GAR erotema 2 — why Adam to posterity, not reverse
pass_a_gloss: Second erotema from GAR: why charge Adam's fall to the line rather than the line's sins back onto Adam? He answers first by radical and seminal presence of all posterity in Adam—not the reverse. He answers second by defining imputation as laying on a penalty: in nature's order penalty trails sin and never runs ahead, so Adam could not suffer for deeds not yet there; bearing and expiating human sin belongs to Christ.
pass_b_english: GAR. It is asked second: Why is Adam's sin rather imputed to posterity than posterity's to Adam? Reply 1. This is because all posterity were in Adam radically and seminarily. Adam was not in posterity in this way. 2. That to impute sin is to inflict penalty on account of sin. But penalty always follows sin in the order of nature, never precedes it. Therefore Adam could not pay penalties for sins that did not yet exist, especially since not he, but Christ, ought to bear the sins of men, and by bearing to expiate them.
source_text: GAR. Quaeritur secundo, Cur potius Adami peccatum posteris, quam posterorum Adamo imputatur? Resp. 1. Hoc inde esse, quod posteri omnes in Adamo radicaliter & seminaliter fuerunt. Adamus in posteris hoc modo non fuit. 2. Quod peccatum imputari, est poenam propter peccatum irrogari. Atqui poena peccatum ordine naturae semper insequitur, nunquam antecedit. Non potuit igitur Adamus poenas dare peccatorum, quae nondum erant, praesertim cum non ipse, sed Christus peccata hominum portare debuerit, & portando expiare.
